idiom_name: `record` with positional parameters, init-only properties and `with`
implementation_notes: A C# record with the `record` modifier gets compiler-generated property-by-property equality, `Equals`/`GetHashCode` and `==`/`!=`, and `with` expressions give non-destructive updates, so the classic SeedWork value class (abstract `ValueObject` base with `GetEqualityComponents`, manual `Equals`/`GetHashCode` and operators) is replaced by a one-line declaration. Keep the base-class form when the type must remain a plain class across language versions, when equality must span a hierarchy, or when explicit equality components are needed. A record class is a reference type and still allocates on every copy.
pitfalls: Array and collection members compare by reference, so two records with equal list contents are unequal, and the shared collection is visible through both values.
A `record class` allocates on every copy; allocation-sensitive code should use `readonly record struct`.
Records are only shallowly immutable - nested classes and collections keep their own mutability, and `with` copies references.

variants.name: Readonly record struct
variants.implementation_notes: The `readonly record struct` gives the same compiler-synthesised, reflection-free equality as a record class while storing the value inline, so small values avoid heap allocation and copies stay cheap; positional properties are init-only only when `readonly` is present (a plain `record struct` exposes read-write properties). Prefer it for small values of a few machine words; for larger ones the copying cost and the 16-byte `struct` guidance favour the record class.
pitfalls: Without `readonly`, a `record struct` has read-write positional properties, so the immutability half of the pattern silently disappears.
Boxing a record struct (as `object`, interface or in non-generic collections) allocates a copy, and mutating that copy does not update the original.
Struct equality still uses declared fields, so a mutable reference-type field can change after the value was used as a key.
